label: Match offer itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the match offer object itself.
details: The game does not document it and no game text uses it with this type. The name matches the same-named function on many other GUI types, which all seem to hand back their own object. A match offer is the proposed marriage or concubine arrangement shown in the interaction window.

label: Actor prestige gain
summary: The prestige the match would give to the actor, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the marriage window next to a prestige icon, with a plus sign, as what the character gets from the match. The actor is the character who starts the interaction.

label: Actor prestige breakdown
summary: A text that explains where the actor's prestige from the match comes from.
details: Vanilla puts it under the prestige amount in the marriage tooltip, after a line saying what the character gets.

label: Chance of children text
summary: A text describing how likely the match is to produce children.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of a line in the shared interaction templates, and as a whole game text for the marriage info.

label: Chance of children tooltip
summary: Going by its name, the tooltip text that explains the chance of children from the match.
details: Vanilla uses it as the hover tooltip in the shared interaction templates.

label: Children's house
summary: A text naming the house the children of the match would belong to.
details: Vanilla uses it as a whole text line about the children's house in the marriage window. The concubine text also builds a similar sentence from the secondary actor's house.

label: Inbreeding chance
summary: The chance, as a number, that children of the match are inbred.
details: Vanilla prints it as a percentage in the sentences 'We are related and there is a ... risk of our children being inbred' and the same for 'They'. It only makes sense when the two are related.

label: Inbreeding warning text
summary: A text describing the inbreeding risk of the match.
details: Vanilla puts it behind a warning icon in the match offer's inbreeding warning.

label: Inheritable trait items
summary: Going by its name, the list of traits the children could inherit from the match, for building a list in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of a list in the interaction window, and checks whether it is empty to hide that list. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Recipient prestige gain
summary: The prestige the match would give to the recipient, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the marriage window next to a prestige icon, with a plus sign. The recipient is the character the interaction is aimed at.

label: Recipient prestige breakdown
summary: A text that explains where the recipient's prestige from the match comes from.
details: Vanilla puts it under the prestige amount in the marriage tooltip.

label: Secondary actor
summary: The second character on the actor's side of the match.
details: Vanilla uses it as the context of a part of the marriage notification window, and in the concubine text to get the house of that character (children are born into it). Going by the name, it is the person the actor arranges the match for, for example a ward or relative; the game does not say.

label: Secondary recipient
summary: The second character on the recipient's side of the match.
details: Vanilla uses it as the context of a part of the marriage notification window. Going by its name, it is the counterpart of the secondary actor; the game does not say more.

label: Has inbreeding risk
summary: Whether the match carries a risk of inbred children.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide the inbreeding warning in the interaction window.

label: Has inheritable traits
summary: Whether there are traits the children could inherit from the match.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the trait list when true, and to show an alternative block (through Not) when false.

label: Is same sex
summary: Going by its name, whether the two characters of the match have the same sex.
details: Vanilla uses it with Not to show some parts of the window only for matches that are not same-sex, for example the matrilineal marriage line.

label: Match offer itself
summary: Going by its name, the match offer object itself.
details: No game text uses it with this type. Other types have a function of the same name that game texts pass along as 'the object itself', for example Character.Self, but that is only a hint.

label: Window itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the matchmaker interaction window object itself.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it with this type. The matchmaker window is the one where you pick who to match for a marriage or concubine.

label: Can change actor
summary: Whether the character on the actor's side can be swapped for another.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the change button for the actor in the marriage window.

label: Can change recipient
summary: Whether the character on the recipient's side can be swapped for another.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the change button for the recipient in the marriage and concubine windows.

label: Can revert actor
summary: Whether the actor's side can be put back to the original character.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the revert button for the actor in the marriage window.

label: Can revert recipient
summary: Whether the recipient's side can be put back to the original character.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the revert button for the recipient in the marriage and concubine windows.

label: Can select anybody
summary: Going by its name, whether any character may be picked in the matchmaker window.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the matchmaker interaction window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click of the close button in the marriage and concubine windows. It returns nothing.

label: Actor to match
summary: The character on the actor's side that is being matched.
details: Vanilla uses it as the context for a character display, and compares it with the character shown there (Character.Self) to decide whether to show a part. In the concubine window it gives the picture of that character.

label: Confirmation window
summary: The confirmation window of the interaction, to use as the context of a part of the GUI.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the confirmation part of the marriage and concubine windows. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Character list
summary: The list of characters you can pick from in the matchmaker window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of the candidate list and asks whether it has items, together with the top character item, to show the list area.

label: Recipient to match
summary: The character on the recipient's side that is being matched.
details: Vanilla uses it as the context for a character display, and compares it with the character shown there (Character.Self) to decide whether to show a part.

label: Top character item
summary: The entry pinned at the top of the candidate list.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of one list entry shown above the others in the marriage and concubine windows. The game does not say which character it is.

label: Has picked characters
summary: Whether characters have been picked in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it to show parts of the window once a pick has been made, and with Not to show a hint before that.

label: Has top character item
summary: Whether there is an entry pinned at the top of the candidate list.
details: Vanilla uses it, often with the check that the list has items, to decide whether to show the list area.

label: Is building list
summary: Going by its name, whether the window is still building its candidate list.
details: No game file uses it with this type. The same name on the character selection list is used with Not to show things only when the list is ready, but that is a hint only.

label: Picking secondary actor
summary: Whether the window is now picking the secondary actor.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the part of the marriage window for that choice.

label: Picking secondary recipient
summary: Whether the window is now picking the secondary recipient.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the part of the marriage and concubine windows for that choice.

label: Change or revert actor
summary: Changes the actor's character, or reverts it to the original, when clicked.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click of both the change button and the revert button of the actor in the marriage window. It returns nothing.

label: Change or revert recipient
summary: Changes the recipient's character, or reverts it to the original, when clicked.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click of the recipient's change button in the concubine window. It returns nothing.

label: Clear picks
summary: Clears what was picked in the window, when clicked.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click of a clear button in the marriage window. It returns nothing; going by its name, it resets the picks.

label: Click actor to match
summary: Going by its name, reacts to a click on the actor's portrait in the matchmaker window.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it. It returns nothing.

label: Click recipient to match
summary: Going by its name, reacts to a click on the recipient's portrait in the matchmaker window.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it. It returns nothing.

label: Rebuild list
summary: Going by its name, rebuilds the candidate list of the matchmaker window.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it. It returns nothing.

label: Window itself
summary: Going by its name, the matchmaker interaction window object itself.
details: No game text uses it with this type. Other types have a function of the same name that game texts pass along as 'the object itself', but that is only a hint.

label: Send interaction
summary: Going by its name, sends the interaction, when clicked.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click of a button in the shared interaction templates. It returns nothing.

label: Trait info itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the trait info object itself.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it with this type. A matchmaker trait info is one trait entry in the match offer's list of inheritable traits.

label: Can upgrade
summary: Whether the trait could be passed on in a stronger form.
details: Vanilla uses it to show an upgrade marker, and with the guaranteed check to show a 'guaranteed and cannot go higher' marker. The exact meaning of upgrading comes from the name and these uses only.

label: Trait's character
summary: The character the trait entry belongs to.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the interaction template, so that character functions work there. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Inheritance info
summary: A text that tells how the trait is inherited by the children.
details: Vanilla uses it as the whole text of a trait entry's inheritance line.

label: The trait
summary: The trait this entry is about.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the interaction template, so that trait functions (name, icon) work there. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Is guaranteed
summary: Whether the trait is certain to be inherited.
details: Vanilla combines it with the can-upgrade check to show a marker when the trait is guaranteed and cannot be upgraded.

label: Trait info itself
summary: Going by its name, the trait info object itself.
details: No game text uses it with this type. Other types have a function of the same name that game texts pass along as 'the object itself', but that is only a hint.

label: Material itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the material object itself.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it with this type. It belongs to the game's internal GUI library.

label: Material texture
summary: The diffuse (base colour) texture of a terrain material, used as its picture.
details: Part of the engine's map editor, where materials are the ground textures painted on the map. Vanilla shows it as the material's icon in the materials list, the material browser, the mix brush and the eyedropper tooltip. The game does not register its return type.

label: Material name
summary: The name of a terrain material of the map editor, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it next to the material's icon and as its tooltip in the materials list, the material browser, the mix brush and the eyedropper tooltip.

label: Material thumbnail
summary: A small preview picture of a terrain material of the map editor.
details: Vanilla shows it at the end of each row of the materials list, on a black background and mirrored upside down. The game does not register its return type.

label: Is highlighted
summary: Whether a terrain material is highlighted in the map editor.
details: Vanilla shows it as the state of the Highlight check box in the materials list. What the highlight does on the map is not shown.

label: Is material locked
summary: Whether a terrain material is locked in the map editor.
details: A locked material may not be changed on the map, as the lock box's tooltip in the mix brush says. Vanilla shows it as the Lock check box in the materials list, puts a faint lock over the material's icon in the eyedropper and greys out its name there.

label: Is material selected
summary: Whether a terrain material is selected in the map editor's materials list.
details: Vanilla shows it as the pressed state of the material's row in the list, and the eyedropper tooltip writes the names of selected materials in bold yellow.

label: Material itself
summary: The terrain material itself, to hand it to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it to the map editor's functions that reload a material from disk and that check or toggle a material in the material browser. The game does not register its return type.

label: Toggle highlight
summary: Switches the highlight of a terrain material on or off; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the Highlight check box in the map editor's materials list. What the highlight does on the map is not shown.

label: Toggle material lock
summary: Locks a terrain material, or unlocks it if it is locked; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the Lock check box in the materials list and from the lock box of a material in the mix brush. A locked material may not be changed on the map.

label: Toggle material selected
summary: Selects a terrain material in the materials list, or deselects it if it is selected; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it when the material's row in the map editor's materials list is clicked.

label: Browser itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the material browser object itself.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it with this type. It belongs to the game's internal GUI library.

label: Apply material choice
summary: Applies the material picked in the map editor's material browser; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the browser's Apply button, which is enabled only while a material is selected.

label: Cancel material browser
summary: Closes the map editor's material browser without applying a choice; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the browser's Cancel button, next to Apply.

label: Current material
summary: The material currently picked in the map editor's material browser.
details: Its kind is Promote, so the Material functions can follow it. Vanilla shows its texture as a large preview beside the list while a material is selected.

label: Shown materials
summary: The list of materials the map editor's material browser shows.
details: Vanilla fills the browser's grid of material buttons from it, three per row. Going by its name and the browser's search box, it is the list after the search filter. The game does not register its return type.

label: Material search text
summary: The text in the search box of the map editor's material browser.
details: The box's tooltip says keywords are separated by spaces and the search ignores upper and lower case.

label: Is a material picked
summary: Whether a material is picked in the map editor's material browser.
details: Vanilla shows the preview picture and enables the Apply button only then.

label: Is material disabled
summary: Whether the given material cannot be picked in the map editor's material browser.
details: Vanilla disables the material's button when it is true. What makes a material disabled is not shown.

label: Is material picked
summary: Whether the given material is picked in the map editor's material browser.
details: Vanilla shows it as the checked state of the material's button in the browser.

label: Browser itself
summary: Going by its name, the material browser object itself.
details: No game text uses it with this type. Other types have a function of the same name that game texts pass along as 'the object itself', but that is only a hint.

label: Set material search
summary: Applies the text of the material browser's search box as its filter; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it each time the text in the box changes. The game lists no argument, so the typed text reaches it in a way the game does not document.

label: Toggle material picked
summary: Picks the given material in the material browser, or unpicks it if it is picked; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it when the material's button in the map editor's material browser is clicked.

label: Entry itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the material entry object itself.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it with this type. It is part of the game's internal GUI library.

label: Entry's material
summary: The material of one entry of a material sample in the map editor's eyedropper.
details: Its kind is Promote, so the Material functions can follow it. Vanilla uses it for the entry's name, texture, lock icon and selected highlight in the eyedropper.

label: Raw value
summary: A whole number for one entry of a material sample in the map editor's eyedropper.
details: Vanilla shows it in the corner of the material's icon and greys out the entry when it is 0 or less. Going by its name, it is the amount before it is turned into the percentage that the value function gives; the game does not say its range.

label: Material share
summary: The share of one material in a material sample of the map editor's eyedropper, as a percentage.
details: Vanilla shows it in a progress bar from 0 to 100 and as text followed by a % sign, in the tooltip about the materials under the mouse.

label: Is entry shown
summary: Whether an entry of a material sample is shown in the map editor's eyedropper tooltip.
details: Vanilla hides the entry's row when it is false. Which entries are hidden is not shown.

label: Entry itself
summary: Going by its name, the material entry object itself.
details: No game text uses it with this type. Other types have a function of the same name that game texts pass along as 'the object itself', but that is only a hint.

label: Mix entries
summary: The entries of a material mix: each material in it with its share.
details: Part of the engine's map editor, where a material mix (a sample of the mix brush) blends several materials. Vanilla fills the mix's rows of sliders and the row of material icons in its header from it, in the mix brush and the smart brush. The game does not register its return type.

label: Mix itself
summary: The material mix itself, to hand it to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it, together with a mix entry, to the functions that change an entry's share or remove a material from the mix, in the mix brush and the smart brush. The game does not register its return type.

label: Can add material
summary: Going by its name, whether another material can be added to the mix.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it.

label: Mix entries
summary: The entries of a material mix: each material in it with its share.
details: Vanilla fills the mix's info tooltip from it, one line per material with its name and percentage. The game does not register its return type.

label: Material count
summary: How many materials a material mix has.
details: Vanilla disables an entry's share slider when the mix has only one material (and when the entry is locked).

label: Mix name
summary: The name of a material mix of the map editor, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the mix's header in the mix brush's sample list and as the title of its info tooltip.

label: Is mix saved
summary: Whether a material mix of the mix brush is persistent, that is, kept when samples are saved.
details: The tooltip of its check box says only persistent samples are saved. Vanilla shows it as that box's state and draws the box's save icon faint when it is false.

label: Mix itself
summary: The material mix itself, to hand it to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it to the mix brush's functions that save, rename, delete, select a sample and lock or edit its entries. The game does not register its return type.

label: Set entry share
summary: Sets the share of one material in a material mix; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it when the entry's slider (0 to 256) moves, in the mix brush and the smart brush. It passes the mix entry, not a number, so going by this use the new value comes from the slider.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The mix entry whose share changes.
fields.values: a material mix entry; vanilla passes `MaterialMixEntry.Self`

label: Toggle persistence
summary: Going by its name, switches the mix between persistent and not persistent.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it. It returns nothing.

label: Mix brush samples
summary: The samples (saved material mixes) of the map editor's mix brush.
details: Vanilla fills the mix brush's samples list from it, one foldable block per mix. The game does not register its return type.

label: Brush itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the material mix brush object itself.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it with this type.

label: Change entry share
summary: Changes the share of one material in a sample of the mix brush; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it when the player finishes typing a value into the entry's text box. The typed text itself is not an argument.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.values: a material mix entry; vanilla passes `MaterialMixEntry.Self`

label: Delete sample
summary: Deletes the given sample from the mix brush; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the Delete button in the sample's header.

label: End share edit
summary: Called when the player lets go of an entry's share slider in a sample of the mix brush; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it when dragging the slider ends; a matching function runs when it starts. What it does then is not shown.

label: Sample under mouse
summary: The material sample under the mouse while the mix brush is sampling.
details: Its kind is Promote and it gives a MaterialsSample. Vanilla uses it for a tooltip that follows the mouse and lists the materials at that point; the mix brush samples with Alt and the left mouse button.

label: Is sampling
summary: Whether the mix brush is taking a sample from the map.
details: Vanilla shows the tooltip with the materials under the mouse only while it is true. The brush's hint text says Alt and the left mouse button sample.

label: Is sample selected
summary: Whether the given sample is selected in the mix brush.
details: Vanilla shows it as the pressed state of the sample's header in the samples list.

label: Rename sample
summary: Opens the map editor's dialog for renaming a material sample.
details: The game's own description says 'Map Editor - Rename Material Sample Dialog'. It takes one input, which is going by the name the sample to rename. It returns nothing. No game file uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not described by the game; going by the name, the sample to rename.

label: Samples
summary: Going by its name, the list of samples of the brush.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Brush itself
summary: Going by its name, the material mix brush object itself.
details: No game text uses it with this type. Other types have a function of the same name that game texts pass along as 'the object itself', but that is only a hint.

label: Start share edit
summary: Called when the player starts dragging an entry's share slider in a sample of the mix brush; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it when dragging the slider starts; a matching function runs when it ends. What it does then is not shown.

label: Toggle share lock
summary: Locks the share of one material in a sample of the mix brush, or unlocks it; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the entry's padlock box ('Lock the percentage of this material.'). A locked entry's slider and text box are disabled.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The entry to lock or unlock.
fields.values: a material mix entry; vanilla passes `MaterialMixEntry.Self`

label: Toggle sample saving
summary: Switches whether the given sample of the mix brush is persistent; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the sample's save check box. Its tooltip says only persistent samples are saved.

label: Toggle sample selected
summary: Selects the given sample of the mix brush, or deselects it if it is selected; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it when the sample's header in the samples list is clicked.

label: Entry's material
summary: The material of one entry of a material mix, to act on it.
details: Its kind is Promote, so the Material functions can follow it. Vanilla uses it to lock or unlock the material from the entry's lock box in the mix brush.

label: Entry itself
summary: The material mix entry itself, to hand it to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it to the smart brush's function that opens the material browser to swap the entry's material for another one. The game does not register its return type.

label: Entry's material
summary: The material of one entry of a material mix.
details: Its kind is Promote, so the Material functions can follow it. Vanilla uses it for the entry's icon, name, tooltip and lock state in the mix brush and the smart brush.

label: Share in percent
summary: The share of one material in a material mix, as a percentage.
details: Vanilla shows it after the material's name in brackets with a % sign, in the mix's info tooltip and in the icon tooltips of its header.

label: Entry value
summary: The value of one entry of a material mix, as a decimal number.
details: Vanilla uses it as the value of the entry's slider, which runs from 0 to 256, in the mix brush and the smart brush. The percentage has its own function.

label: Entry value text
summary: The value of one entry of a material mix, written as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the edit box beside the entry's slider, where the player can also type a new value.

label: Is share locked
summary: Whether the share of one material in a material mix is locked.
details: Vanilla shows it as the padlock box 'Lock the percentage of this material.' and disables the entry's slider and edit box while it is true.

label: Entry itself
summary: The material mix entry itself, to hand it to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it to the functions that set an entry's share, change it from typed text, lock it or remove it from the mix. The game does not register its return type.

label: Set percentage value
summary: Going by its name, sets the entry's share of the mix as a percentage.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not described by the game; going by the name, the new percentage.

label: Toggle locked
summary: Going by its name, locks the entry, or unlocks it if it is locked.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it. It returns nothing.

label: Blur threshold
summary: The blur threshold setting of the material brush, for its slider.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data of the blur threshold slider, which is shown only while the blur tool is selected. The game does not register its return type.

label: Painting mode itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the painting mode object itself.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it with this type.

label: Focus camera on error
summary: Moves the map editor's camera to a material error; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the button 'Focus camera on material error.' of the material brush. While a search runs, the button shows a spinner. What counts as a material error is not shown.

label: Is blur tool selected
summary: Whether the blur tool of the material brush is selected.
details: The blur tool blurs all materials within the brush radius. Vanilla shows it as the tool button's state and shows the blur threshold slider only while it is true.

label: Shared brush settings
summary: Whether all material painting tools use the same brush settings.
details: Vanilla shows it as the state of the brush settings lock button, whose tooltip says that when it is on, all material painting tools use the same global brush settings. A click sets the opposite state.

label: Is eraser selected
summary: Whether the material eraser tool is selected.
details: Vanilla shows it as the pressed state of the 'Material Eraser' button.

label: Is eyedropper selected
summary: Whether the eyedropper of the material brush is selected.
details: Vanilla shows it as the state of the material brush's eyedropper button.

label: Is paint brush selected
summary: Whether the material paint brush tool is selected.
details: Vanilla shows it as the pressed state of the 'Material Paint Brush' button.

label: Can paint
summary: Whether the material brush can paint at the moment.
details: Vanilla shows the brush settings and the pixel snap button only while it is true. When it is false, the map view's tooltip says 'Select material first!'.

label: Is searching for error
summary: Whether the material brush is searching for a material error.
details: While it is true, vanilla hides the icon of the 'Focus camera on material error.' button and shows a spinner there instead.

label: Is material brush active
summary: Whether the material brush is the active tool of the engine's map editor.
details: Vanilla shows it as the pressed state of the toolbar button 'Material Brush'.

label: Trim while painting
summary: Whether materials are trimmed automatically while the paint brush is used.
details: Vanilla shows it as the state of the trim-while-painting button; a click sets the opposite state. Trimming removes materials that exceed the trimmer's limit.

label: Is trimmer selected
summary: Whether the material trimmer tool is selected.
details: The trimmer erases all materials that exceed the given limit. Vanilla shows it as the pressed state of the trimmer button.

label: Reload materials
summary: Reloads all material textures from disk; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the material brush's reload button ('Reload all material textures from disk'). A single material can be reloaded from the materials list instead.

label: Select blur tool
summary: Makes the blur tool the material brush's current tool; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the blur button, whose tooltip says the tool blurs all materials within the brush radius and can also be used at any time by holding Shift.

label: Select eraser
summary: Makes the material eraser the material brush's current tool; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the 'Material Eraser' button.

label: Select eyedropper
summary: Makes the eyedropper the material brush's current tool; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the material brush's eyedropper button.

label: Select paint brush
summary: Makes the paint brush the material brush's current tool; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the 'Material Paint Brush' button.

label: Select trimmer
summary: Makes the trimmer the material brush's current tool; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the trimmer button, whose tooltip says the trimmer erases all materials that exceed the given limit.

label: Painting mode itself
summary: Going by its name, the painting mode object itself.
details: No game text uses it with this type. Other types have a function of the same name that game texts pass along as 'the object itself', but that is only a hint.

label: Share brush settings
summary: Switches whether all material painting tools use the same brush settings; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the brush settings lock button with the opposite of the current state, so a click toggles it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Whether the tools share one set of brush settings.
fields.values: yes or no (vanilla passes the opposite of the current state)

label: Set trim while painting
summary: Switches automatic trimming of materials while painting on or off; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the trim-while-painting button with the opposite of the current state, so a click toggles it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Whether materials are trimmed while painting.
fields.values: yes or no (vanilla passes the opposite of the current state)

label: Materials itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the materials object itself.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it with this type.

label: Materials list
summary: Going by its name, the list of materials.
details: No game file uses it with this type. The same name on other types is used as list data and for counting items, but that is only a hint. The game documents no return type for it.

label: Materials list
summary: The list of terrain materials of the map editor.
details: Vanilla fills the map editor's materials list from it, one row per material with its lock, highlight, name and pictures. The game does not register its return type.

label: Select first
summary: Going by its name, selects the first material of the list.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it. It returns nothing.

label: Select last
summary: Going by its name, selects the last material of the list.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it. It returns nothing.

label: Select next
summary: Going by its name, selects the material after the current one.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it. It returns nothing.

label: Select previous
summary: Going by its name, selects the material before the current one.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it. It returns nothing.

label: Materials itself
summary: Going by its name, the materials object itself.
details: No game text uses it with this type. Other types have a function of the same name that game texts pass along as 'the object itself', but that is only a hint.

label: Toggle highlight
summary: Going by its name, switches the highlight of the current material on or off.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle locked
summary: Going by its name, locks the current material, or unlocks it if it is locked.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it. It returns nothing.

label: Sample itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the materials sample object itself.
details: The game documents nothing more and no game file uses it with this type.

label: Sample entries
summary: The entries of a material sample: each material found at a point of the map, with its share.
details: Vanilla fills the tooltip about the materials under the mouse from it, one row per material. The game does not register its return type.

label: Sample X
summary: A whole number shown as the first of two numbers at the top of a material sample's tooltip.
details: Vanilla writes it as '[X] x [Y]' above the list of materials under the mouse. Going by its name, it is the sample point's X coordinate; the game does not say in what units.

label: Sample Y
summary: A whole number shown as the second of two numbers at the top of a material sample's tooltip.
details: Vanilla writes it as '[X] x [Y]' above the list of materials under the mouse. Going by its name, it is the sample point's Y coordinate; the game does not say in what units.

label: Sample itself
summary: Going by its name, the materials sample object itself.
details: No game text uses it with this type. Other types have a function of the same name that game texts pass along as 'the object itself', but that is only a hint.
